content: Oṃ! May all be auspicious!In the perfect land of Bengal,Of the noble Zahor royal lineage,Descended from the Bodhisattva Śāntarakṣita,I pray at the feet of Dīpaṃkara.Skilled and respectful in serving father and mother,Beautiful in form, charming, wise, and compassionate,Tamed, gentle-natured, skillful in means, and of great courage,I pray at the feet of Dīpaṃkara.Learned in all worldly treatises,And in the various arts of craftsmanship and medicine,Skilled in all the Vedas, with vast and expansive knowledge,I pray at the feet of Dīpaṃkara.Without attachment to the qualities of sensory desire,Having renounced the abundant wealth of the kingdom,He became a monk of the Mahāsāṃghika order;I pray to the glorious Atiśa.As taught in the four sections of the Vinaya Piṭaka,Regarding the trainings prescribed by the Sugata,He was completely pure, untainted by the faults of transgression;I pray to the glorious Atiśa.Having relied upon many learned masters,And being skilled in the Tripitaka, grammar, and logic,With vast knowledge of all the pith instructions,I pray to the glorious Atiśa.From the guru who protects the earth, the King of Suvarṇadvīpa,Having received the nectar-medicine of bodhicitta,He acted for the benefit of all wandering beings;I pray to the glorious Atiśa.For sentient beings who are destitute and in extreme suffering,With a heart of love for the vast multitude,To the sole protector and father of the world,Including gods, asuras, and humans, I pray.From the holy guru who has attained realization,Having received the oral transmission of the yidam deity’s visualization,By making one-pointed practice the heart essence,I pray to you who attained the prophecy.Mindful of those to be tamed who were in Tibet,You traveled to the Land of Snows,And served as the guru to the great leaders and their communities;To you, worthy of honor and respect, I pray.Had a supreme scholar like you not come to Tibet,Even though the Buddha’s teachings might have existed,Most would have remained ignorant of the profound meaning;To you who taught it so well, I pray.By translating treatises and revising those already translated,By explaining their meaning and composing your own works,By skillfully guiding others onto the authentic path,To you who caused the teachings to flourish, I pray.You entered the path that turns away from wrong views,Subdued the Maras, Tīrthikas, and the tenets of Īśvara,And by logic defeated them, placing them on the path to liberation;To you, the guide for those desiring liberation, I pray.Generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and diligence,Meditative concentration and wisdom—the six perfections;Through repeated practice over countless lifetimes,To you who have fully perfected the two accumulations, I pray.Giving what is needed, speaking with pleasant words,Acting in harmony with the world for the sake of those to be tamed,Through the splendor of the four means of gathering,To you who are devoted to the benefit of others, I pray.Faith, ethical discipline, learning, and generosity,A sense of shame, moral dread, and wisdom—You are the treasury enriched with these seven noble riches;To you, the source of all qualities, I pray.Supreme disciple who made aspiration prayers in the past,When you, the source of the Victors, arrived from afar,"My Upāsaka has arrived today," you said;To you who possess the divine eye and clairvoyance, I pray.From Magadha, the devoted disciplePlayed cymbals and offered prayers, the sound of whichYou heard in Tibet and sent word to 'Brom;To you who possess the clairvoyance of the divine ear, I pray.When divine music resounded in Lhasa,You arrived swiftly to the assembly of deities in the temple,And offered prostrations and circumambulations in the sky;To you who possess miraculous powers and clairvoyance, I pray.Where the King’s testament was hidden as a treasure,The ḍākinīs revealed to you the place to open the cache;The Jowo Śākyamuni is here through your kindness;To you, the gracious Lord, I pray.For those afflicted by the diseases of the earth-lords,The various protective cycles for sustaining lifeAlso arose from you, who heal the illnesses of beings;To you, renowned as the second Nāgārjuna, I pray.When you resided upon the sands at Nyethang Or,Indra and the hosts of gods in the skySent down a rain of flowers of the five precious kinds;To you, the Guru, the God of Gods, I pray.At Yorpo Ching-ru, a maiden offered her head ornament;Hearing of her death, you performed the purification of her obscurations;You declared that the noble daughter had been reborn as a deity;To you, the Guide of Beings, I pray."I am departing from here to the realm of Tuṣita;Those who have faith and devotion toward meShall meet me in the realm of Tuṣita," you declared;To you, who see the future directly, I pray.In the realm of Tuṣita, you are Vimalākāśa;In the land of the Āryas, you are Dīpaṃkaraśrī;In this Land of Snows, you are the glorious Atiśa;To you, whose fame pervades the earth, I pray.I, Dromtönpa, built the Reting temple;Because I prayed to guide all beings,From the realm of Tuṣita, you scattered flowers of consecration;To you who arrived in person with blessings, I pray.Having seen and heard of your qualities,With a faithful heart, I call out in prayer;From the realm of Tuṣita, look upon me with compassion,And just as I have prayed, please grant your blessings.Still, in this Land of Snows, there are manyWho have faith in you and follow your path;Keep them in your heart, and like a mother to her child,I pray you act with love as my spiritual friend.Beings of this degenerate age are like the blind,Having been taken under the care of false spiritual friends;Those without a guide in the abyss of cyclic existence,I pray you swiftly draw them with the hook of your compassion.At all times and in every situation,Since you, holy one, are my protector,I shall swiftly attain complete and perfect buddhahood;I pray you bestow upon me the three of hearing, contemplation, and meditation.Spiritual friend of all, my protector,Heir to the Victors, successor of the Conquerors,Precious source of welfare for self and others,At the feet of the teacher, my spiritual friend, I pray.Through the power of familiarizing with the two accumulations for countless eons,The mandala of your wisdom, knowing the meaning of the three spheres, has expanded;Foremost among the spiritual sons of Atiśa,At the feet of Legs-pa'i-shes-rab, I pray.Dīpaṃkara, glorious father of all the Victors,From the ocean of Victors, the source of the Victors,You extracted the essence of the instructions and brought satisfaction;At the feet of Brtson-'grus-g.yung-drung, I pray.Po-to-ba, in whose heart the urgency of impermanence arose,Spyan-snga-ba, who meditated on cherishing others more than oneself,Phu-chung-ba, who made spiritual practice the heart essence,To the three spiritual brothers, the heirs of the Victors, I pray.In all my lives, may I never be parted from the Lord Atiśa and his spiritual heirs,And may I enjoy the splendor of the Dharma;Having fully perfected the qualities of the stages and paths,May I swiftly attain the state of Vajradhara.
